title: "Week 0 · Prerequisites"
subtitle: "What to refresh before the first lectures, and the additional reading list"
---

The programme assumes undergraduate statistics. The prerequisites sheet lists
the concepts each of the first three weeks builds on and points to pre-recorded
lectures on Ilias and to Khan Academy units for anyone who needs to close a gap.
A second sheet, distributed to the 2024/25 cohort, names the two handbooks the
lectures follow and a few additions.

## What the prerequisites sheet covers

**Before Week 1.** Mean, median, mode, maximum, minimum, quantiles, quartiles
and percentiles; box plot and histogram; distribution, skew and kurtosis;
powers and the logarithm transformation. Four pre-recorded Ilias lectures
(introduction to statistics and scale levels; basic measures; understanding and
visualising data I and II) and Khan Academy units on summarising and displaying
quantitative data and on logarithms.

**Before Week 2.** Mean, variance and standard deviation; probability; the
normal distribution and confidence intervals. Three pre-recorded Ilias lectures
(probability; statistical distributions; confidence intervals) and Khan Academy
units on variance, standard deviation and basic probability.

**Before Week 3.** Optional only: the Khan Academy module on modelling data
distributions, in particular percentiles, z-scores, and the normal distribution
with the empirical rule.

## What the additional literature sheet covers

Two key handbooks, with the chapters the lectures draw on, and three additions:

-   📖 **OpenIntro Statistics** (Diez, Çetinkaya-Rundel and Barr, 2019):
    sampling principles and strategies, experiments, summarising data, defining
    probability and the law of large numbers, random variables, continuous
    distributions, the normal distribution, inference for numerical data, and
    the introduction to linear regression.
-   📖 **Mastering 'Metrics: the path from cause to effect** (Angrist and
    Pischke, 2015): Chapter 1, Randomized Trials, and Chapter 2, Regression.
-   📖 **Fundamentals of Data Visualization** (Wilke, 2019), Part I chapters 6
    to 9 on visualising distributions.
-   📖 Our World in Data on the Gini coefficient and on the history of global
    economic inequality.

The full list with links is on the [reading list](../resources.qmd) page.
